description: We’re a core trio covering data, backend, and UX: Boris handles NASA satellite data and visualization; Abel builds the backend pipelines; and James shapes the math models and interactive mechanics. Together, we’re turning climate data into an intuitive rotation simulator for farmers
summary:
Farmers on the  northern coast of Peru  normally face challenges when it is about choosing crops due to droughts, irrigation needs and unpredictable El Niño rainfall. Although NASA provides valuable satellite data, understanding it can be difficult, however with a understandable interface witch converts data into these data into data which is easy to catch.
That's why Field Shift transforms this information into simple visuals and practical agricultural recommendations. Farmers can select their district or outline their fields, while Sprout, an alien-cat guide, helps them explore two sections.

“Today” displays current climate, soil and vegetation conditions, comparing four crop rotation strategies. “What’s Ahead” uses two XGBoost models trained on 28 years of historical data to predict soil moisture and vegetation, simulate drought and El Niño scenarios, and identify areas with better water availability.

The platform explains each recommendation, including its benefits, costs and risks. Farmers can prioritize water conservation, income, soil health, pest control or climate resilience.

Available in English, Spanish and Quechua (beta), Field Shift is free, mobile-friendly and offers simple and professional viewing modes. It supports informed decisions without replacing farmers or agronomists.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

Field Shift is a platform that combines NASA satellite data, soil information and crop characteristics to help farmers make better planting decisions. Users can select their location, explore current environmental conditions, compare four crop rotation strategies and simulate future scenarios such as droughts and El Niño events. Sprout, an original alien-cat guide, helps users navigate the platform.

What are its benefits?

It helps farmers save water, improve soil health, reduce agricultural risks and identify more profitable crop alternatives. It also makes complex scientific information easier to understand through simple visuals and personalized recommendations.

What is the expected impact of the project?

Field Shift aims to strengthen agriculture in Lambayeque by helping farming communities adapt to climate change, manage water resources more efficiently and adopt more sustainable agricultural practices.

What tools, programming languages and software were used?

The project uses Vue 3, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet and D3 for the interface. Python, FastAPI and XGBoost power the data processing and predictive models. NASA data services, Google Earth Engine, Docker and Caddy support data integration and deployment.

What makes the project creative?

Its main innovation is transforming complex satellite observations into practical agricultural guidance. It combines an interactive alien-cat guide, two visualization modes (Farmer and Pro), climate simulations and recommendations that adapt to each farmer's priorities.

What factors did the team consider?

The team considered northern Peru's climate, El Niño events, water availability, soil conditions, crop requirements and farmers' priorities. It also accounted for satellite data limitations and prediction accuracy, ensuring transparency and emphasizing that the platform supports, rather than replaces, farmers' experience and agronomists' expertise.
